prediction_scored: miss. E = 0.931% (-2.35 to 4.323). refute_if (upper bound below +5.0%) is met, by 0.68 points, which is less than one standard error (1.7 points), so it is met within sampling error (rule 10). support_if (E >= 2% and lower bound above 0) is not met. The predicted lengthening of about 5%, about 35 seconds on an 11.5-minute trip, is excluded; a lengthening of up to 4.3% (about 30 seconds) is not.
settle: Corridor-level volume counts on 12th to 18th Streets before and after, and a second winter (2020-21 is unusable because of the pandemic), would separate a small lengthening from none. Door-to-door times answer the traveller's question; DOT's probe runs on single streets answer the street's question, and the two agree that the change was small.

research_needed.question: Did traffic volume on 14th Street fall by more than it rose on 12th, 13th and 15th to 18th Streets (evaporation)?
research_needed.data: Automated or manual counts on each crosstown street from 2nd to 10th Avenue for at least two months before and after; DOT's own ATR counts behind the Sam Schwartz reports are not in 7ym2-wayt (four 2019 locations only).
research_needed.design: Before-after with control streets in Midtown; publish the counts.

research_needed.question: Was the small rise in trip distance a detour caused by the busway or the continuation of a drift that began in 2018?
research_needed.data: TLC trip records with GPS traces (not public since mid-2016) or app-company route data; taxi zone pairs at finer scale.
research_needed.design: Route-level comparison of the share of crosstown trips using 14th Street before and after.

research_needed.question: Did the busway change injuries on 14th Street and its parallel streets, and NO2 along the corridor?
research_needed.data: h9gi-nx95 crashes by street segment; NYCCAS street-level monitors on 14th Street (if any) or low-cost sensors.
research_needed.design: Registered before-after with control corridors, segment-level counts.

research_needed.question: The System Public Graph holds no finding on road-space reallocation, traffic evaporation or displaced traffic.
research_needed.data: Transport literature (Cairns et al. 1998, 2002; Nello-Deakin 2022; bus-lane evaluations) is outside the graph's health-centred corpus.

notes: The claim was registered as a conflict: it bet that removing through traffic from 14th Street would lengthen crosstown trips by about 5%, against the evaporation literature and DOT's summary. The verdict 'contested' means that bet lost: the data agree with the research side. Secondary estimates, not deciding: all busway hours (06-21, every day) 0.793% (-3.534 to 5.315); overnight (22-05, busway not in force) -1.326% (-5.033 to 2.525). The plain year-over-year DiD with a day bootstrap gives 0.796% (-0.957 to 2.624) on weekdays; the same estimator gave +3.4% in the placebo year 2017-18 to 2018-19, so its bootstrap interval understates the year-to-year noise. Exploratory: the monthly year-over-year contrast was +4.4% in October 2019 and +3.0% in November, then -2.8%, -1.3% and -1.1% in December to February. The pre-busway monthly values have a standard deviation of 2.3%, so the pattern of early lengthening followed by adaptation is suggestive and not established. Weekday daytime trips between the treated zones averaged 11.52 minutes and 1.257 miles in October 2018 to February 2019 (128,579 trips) and 11.41 minutes and 1.289 miles in October 2019 to February 2020 (102,600 trips). Control-group sensitivity of the weekday estimate (exploratory): against Midtown pairs only, duration -0.2% (-4.22 to 3.97) and distance -0.12%; against downtown pairs only, duration 2.53% (-1.21 to 6.42) and distance 0.6% (-0.82 to 2.04). The registered estimator has no resampling, so rule 9 does not apply. Placebo seasons 2017 and 2018 were recomputed with the post months included and are unchanged.
notes_referee: Referee reproduced +0.93% (-2.35 to +4.32). Verdict stands. Exploratory split: pairs north of 14th St +7.4% (+2.8 to +12.1), southern pairs -1.5%; against downtown controls alone refute_if is not met. The pooled estimate is an average over pairs, many of which may not use 14th Street.
